answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The sonnet multiplier is published, charged in gale, and thread lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2643 identities would post 1841 proofs and burn roughly 26 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
